@pcbeingused333 Good fix, there was a "panic" corner case, and I am trying to clean those up as much as possible.

Below is what my AI Review gave me (Sol + Opus).

Not sure all of it needs to be fixed or is even an issue, but at least the panic bulletproofing should be.

> Note: Existing code might have those issues, but those will be in different PRs. Just making sure new code is more strict.

--- AI Feedback:
````md
## Request: Write the PR 372 comment with findings and needed fix

### User Ask

Write a `## PR Comment` section that explains the findings on PR 372 and the fix needed before merge. Code files are not updated.

### Notes

- The comment below follows the reconciled verdict from the previous request: merge after small changes.

- It is written to be pasted as-is on the GitHub PR.

## PR Comment

Thanks for this fix. Losing every tool call from providers that omit `index` (Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint) is a real problem, and isolating the routing in a small `ToolCallSlots` helper is a good approach. The public API is unchanged, and providers that send `index` behave exactly as before.

A few issues need to be addressed before we can merge.

### 1. New unchecked arithmetic on provider input (panic)

- `ToolCallSlots::slot` runs `self.started.max(index + 1)`, where `index` is any `u32` sent by the provider.

- On 32-bit targets (for example `wasm32`), `index == u32::MAX` overflows `usize`. Debug builds, and so `cargo test`, panic; release builds wrap to `0`.

- `slot()` now runs for every delta, even when `capture_tool_calls` is off. Before this PR, the only `index + 1` was inside `capture_tool_call`, after the capture check. So this panic path is new.

### 2. Unbounded provider index (existing, but please bound it here)

- `capture_tool_call` calls `calls.resize(index + 1, ...)`. A huge `index` (for example `4_000_000_000`) triggers a very large allocation, which can lead to a capacity panic or an out-of-memory abort.

- This problem already existed. Since this PR now owns slot selection, it is the right place to bound the index once, before any arithmetic or allocation.

### 3. Interleaved ids without `index` corrupt calls

- With deltas for calls `a`, `b`, then `a` again, the slots are `0`, `1`, `2`, because only `last_id` is tracked.

- The third delta should continue call `a`. Instead, it creates a third call with a leftover argument fragment. The first `a` call keeps truncated arguments, which stay as a `Value::String` at `[DONE]`.

- This replaces silent loss with silent corruption, and callers get no error.

### 4. Continuation goes to the highest slot, not the last used slot

- After explicit indexes `0`, `1`, `0`, a delta with no `index` and no `id` goes to slot `1`, because `started - 1` is the highest slot seen, not the slot used last.

- This is unlikely in practice, but the fix is cheap.

### Requested changes

- **Bound the slot:** add a cap such as `MAX_TOOL_CALL_SLOTS = 128`. Make `slot()` return `Option<usize>`, and skip the delta (with a `tracing::warn!`) when the slot is out of range. This removes the new overflow and the large `resize` at the same time.

- **Map ids to slots:** keep a `HashMap<String, usize>`, so an id that comes back continues its own call.

- **Track the last used slot:** use `last_slot` for continuations, instead of `started - 1`.

- **Read `id` once:** in `queue_delta_tool_calls`, take `id` once as an `Option<String>` instead of calling both `get("id")` and `x_take("id")`.

- **Document the limitation:** when a provider omits both `index` and `id`, a delta that repeats the function name starts a new call. Note this in the `ToolCallSlots` doc comment.

- **Add a doc comment** to the new `tool_call_slots` field, to match the other fields.

### Suggested shape

```rust
const MAX_TOOL_CALL_SLOTS: usize = 128;

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct ToolCallSlots {
	next: usize,
	last_slot: Option<usize>,
	slot_by_id: HashMap<String, usize>,
}

impl ToolCallSlots {
	/// Returns `None` when the delta cannot be routed safely (slot out of bounds).
	fn slot(&mut self, index: Option<usize>, id: Option<&str>, has_name: bool) -> Option<usize> {
		let id = id.filter(|id| !id.is_empty());
		let slot = match (index, id) {
			(Some(index), _) => index,
			(None, Some(id)) => self.slot_by_id.get(id).copied().unwrap_or(self.next),
			(None, None) => match self.last_slot {
				Some(last_slot) if !has_name => last_slot,
				_ => self.next,
			},
		};
		if slot >= MAX_TOOL_CALL_SLOTS {
			return None;
		}
		if let Some(id) = id {
			self.slot_by_id.entry(id.to_string()).or_insert(slot);
		}
		self.next = self.next.max(slot + 1);
		self.last_slot = Some(slot);
		Some(slot)
	}
}
```

- `slot + 1` is safe here, because `slot` is checked against the cap first.

- Caller side: `let Some(slot) = self.tool_call_slots.slot(...) else { tracing::warn!(...); continue; };`.

### Tests to add

- Interleaved ids without `index`: `a`, `b`, `a` gives `0`, `1`, `0`.

- Mixed indexes: explicit `0`, `1`, `0`, then a delta with no `index` and no `id`, gives `0`.

- Oversized index: `Some(u32::MAX as usize)` gives `None`, and no event is queued.

- Name repeated without an id: pins the documented limitation.

- One end-to-end test that drives the streamer itself. Ideally, a yakbak cassette in `tests/tests_yakbak_openai.rs` with two parallel calls, no `index`, and arguments split across deltas. It should check both the `ToolCallChunk` events and the parsed `fn_arguments` in `StreamEnd`.
````
if this is parsing response bodies, please include a yakbak regression test for the case this fixes

Thanks for the detailed review. 371ad06 addresses each point:

- **Bound the slot:** `MAX_TOOL_CALL_SLOTS = 128`. `slot()` now returns `Option<usize>` and checks the cap before any arithmetic or allocation. An out-of-range delta is skipped with a `tracing::warn!` and leaves the routing state untouched.
- **Map ids to slots:** `slot_by_id: HashMap<String, usize>`, so `a, b, a` without `index` continues call `a`.
- **Last used slot:** continuations use `last_slot`, so `0, 1, 0` followed by a bare delta goes to slot 0.
- **Read `id` once:** `queue_delta_tool_calls` takes `id` a single time with `x_take`.
- **Docs:** the `ToolCallSlots` comment notes the limitation (no `index` and no `id`: a repeated function name starts a new call), and the `tool_call_slots` field has a doc comment.
- **Tests:** unit cases for `a,b,a`, `0,1,0` + bare delta, `u32::MAX`/`usize::MAX`/cap boundary, and the repeated-name limitation. As requested, a yakbak replay `stream_tool_calls_without_index` covers two interleaved calls whose deltas carry only `id`. It fails on the previous commit (5 captured calls instead of 2) and passes now.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

@pcbeingused333 I was going to merge it, but got one YakBak test fail (see below)

So, not sure what the process should be.

@ropoctl as the YakBak expert, what should the process be? The issue is that we do not have access to all providers. So, in this case, the OpenRouter one, what would be the right process?

If it is a code issue, then we can fix it, but if it is a harmless change in the output, would we need to rerun this with the real provider (OpenRouter)?


Yakbak test file
```

---- openrouter_stream_keeps_tool_calls_with_sparse_indexes_apart stdout ----
[yakbak] REPLAY tests/data/yakbak/open_router/tool_call_sparse_index_regression/response_000.txt (1413 bytes, ct=text/event-stream, chunk_size=8192)

 right: [("call_two", "read_file", Object {"path": String("/runbook")}), ("call_seven", "list_dir", Object {}), ("call_max", "stat_file", Object {})]
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace


failures:

```

The YakBak failure is a real code issue in this PR, not a provider output change. The `MAX_TOOL_CALL_SLOTS = 128` cap added in the last round dropped the `call_max` delta (index 4294967295) that `openrouter_stream_keeps_tool_calls_with_sparse_indexes_apart` expects to keep. Since `tool_calls` is a `BTreeMap<u32, _>`, a large index allocates nothing, so the cap is not needed for memory safety. The new commit bounds the slot at `u32::MAX` instead (it must fit the map key; `next` now uses `saturating_add`), and the rest of the routing (`slot_by_id`, `last_slot`, skipping out-of-range) is unchanged. No re-record against OpenRouter is needed: the existing fixture passes as is.

Tests run with cargo in the rust:1.95 image: `tests_yakbak_parser_regressions` 10 passed (the sparse-index test failed before the change) and `cargo test --lib openai::streamer` 18 passed.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

PR Commit message:

```
* - fix(openai): keep streamed tool calls whose deltas omit index

Some OpenAI-compatible servers (e.g. Gemini's) send tool_calls deltas without an
index, and the streamer skipped every such delta, so the calls were lost. Without
an index a delta now starts a new slot when it carries a new id (or a function name
and no id) and otherwise continues the last one; deltas with an index behave as
before.

* fix(openai): bound and route streamed tool call slots safely

Cap the slot at MAX_TOOL_CALL_SLOTS so an untrusted provider index cannot overflow or force a huge allocation, map ids to slots so interleaved calls without index keep their own arguments, and continue the last used slot. Adds unit tests and a yakbak replay test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(openai): cap tool call slots at u32 range, not 128

The tool_calls map is sparse (BTreeMap<u32, _>), so a large provider index
allocates nothing. The 128 cap dropped the legitimate max-index call that the
Yakbak sparse-index regression expects to keep.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```
@pcbeingused333 Thanks for fixing all of the issues.
